Sydney - A show featuring dozens of drones in dazzling displays above Sydney’s Darling Harbour has been called off, organisers said on May 26, after the flying gadgets malfunctioned and fell into the water. Vivid Sydney takes place every year and features drones, fireworks and art shows across the Australian city’s central business district. But a nightly drone show went terribly wrong on May 25 as the airborne objects glitched out and plunged into the harbour. “Are they meant to do that?“ an onlooker asks in one video shared by local news.

In a statement, Vivid said its team “understand this will be disappointing for audiences and appreciate the public’s understanding” but that the technical and safety review had led to the decision to cancel. “Providing certainty for visitors, residents and event attendees as Vivid Sydney continues over the coming weeks has also been an important consideration in making this decision,” Vivid said in a statement. “Fireworks displays will now complement the Laser Lightfall experience in Darling Harbour at the times previously scheduled for drone shows, adding another layer of spectacle to Vivid Sydney’s celebrations. “Public safety remains the absolute priority and all decisions have been guided by expert technical and regulatory advice.”

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Fireworks displays will replace all drone shows at the iconic festival after a technical issue saw dozens fall from the sky on Monday night

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Vivid Sydney has cancelled all remaining drone shows after 83 fell from the sky into Darling Harbour this week, prompting a “full assessment” of the aerial light show.

On Monday, audiences looked on as a performance called Star-Bound suddenly went awry, with “unforeseen technical difficulties” causing 83 drones to plunge into the waters of Cockle Bay and six to land on a boardwalk. No injuries were reported.

Four performances were cancelled on Tuesday and Wednesday as a precaution while operators completed a full technical and safety review. On Saturday, Vivid confirmed all remaining drone shows scheduled for the next two weeks were also cancelled.

In a statement, Vivid said its team “understand this will be disappointing for audiences and appreciate the public’s understanding” but that the technical and safety review had led to the decision to cancel.

“Providing certainty for visitors, residents and event attendees as Vivid Sydney continues over the coming weeks has also been an important consideration in making this decision,” Vivid said in a statement.

“Fireworks displays will now complement the Laser Lightfall experience in Darling Harbour at the times previously scheduled for drone shows, adding another layer of spectacle to Vivid Sydney’s celebrations.

“Public safety remains the absolute priority and all decisions have been guided by expert technical and regulatory advice.”

Skymagic, the UK-based operator of the drone show, said in a statement that an “unforeseen change in the radio frequency environment occurring after take-off” compromised the positional accuracy of the fleet.

“Early indications show there was no foul play present, but we are still investigating all possibilities,” Dyfan Rhys, Skymagic’s head of operations and production, elaborated on Tuesday.

Rhys said despite the dramatic images circulating on social media, the public was not at risk.

While the pilot team managed to lock the main fleet stationary in the air to evaluate the situation, the drones experiencing issues encountered the geofence boundary.

“[They] shut down to preserve the safety zone,” he said, resulting in 83 falling into the harbour and six landing on the foreshore boardwalk.

Vivid Sydney takes place every year and features drones, fireworks and art shows across the Australian city’s central business district.

Sydney - A show featuring dozens of drones in dazzling displays above Sydney’s Darling Harbour has been called off, organisers said on May 26, after the flying gadgets malfunctioned and fell into the water.

Vivid Sydney takes place every year and features drones, fireworks and art shows across the Australian city’s central business district.

But a nightly drone show went terribly wrong on May 25 as the airborne objects glitched out and plunged into the harbour.

“Are they meant to do that?“ an onlooker asks in one video shared by local news.

SkyMagic – the company behind the drone performance – blamed a change in radio frequency for the disaster that saw 89 of the devices fall into Cockle Bay.

And organisers told AFP that “unforeseen technical difficulties” had forced them to call off performances planned for May 26 and 27.

“We apologise for the disappointment and inconvenience caused to attendees.”

No one was hurt and no drones fell outside of a “designated exclusion zone”, organisers said. AFP

payload.title: Vivid Sydney peruu loput drooniesitykset Darling Harbourin häiriön jälkeen
payload.summary: Vivid Sydney on perunut kaikki jäljellä olevat drooniesityksensä, kun kymmenet droonit putosivat Darling Harbourin alueelle teknisen häiriön vuoksi. Esitysten tilalle tuodaan ilotulituksia.
payload.content:
Vivid Sydney on perunut kaikki jäljellä olevat drooniesityksensä sen jälkeen, kun 83 droonia putosi tällä viikolla Darling Harbourin veteen ja kuusi droonia päätyi kävelyalueelle Star-Bound-esityksen aikana. Järjestäjien mukaan päätös tehtiin teknisen ja turvallisuuteen liittyvän arvioinnin jälkeen, eikä tapahtuneesta ole raportoitu henkilövahinkoja.

## Esitys epäonnistui teknisen häiriön vuoksi

Häiriö tapahtui maanantai-iltana Sydneyssä, kun Darling Harbourin yllä järjestetty droonivaloesitys meni äkillisesti pieleen. Esityksen kerrottiin kohdanneen ennalta arvaamattomia teknisiä vaikeuksia, joiden seurauksena suuri määrä drooneja putosi Cockle Bayn veteen. Lisäksi kuusi droonia laskeutui kävelyalueelle.

Vivid Sydney on vuosittain järjestettävä valon, taiteen ja kaupunkitapahtumien festivaali, jonka ohjelmaan kuuluu drooniesitysten lisäksi muun muassa ilotulituksia ja taidekokonaisuuksia Sydneyn keskustassa. Darling Harbourin drooniesitykset olivat osa festivaalin iltaohjelmaa, ja paikalla olleet katsojat näkivät häiriön esityksen aikana.

Tapauksen jälkeen neljä esitystä peruttiin tiistaina ja keskiviikkona varotoimena, kun operaattorit tekivät teknistä ja turvallisuutta koskevaa tarkastusta. Lauantaina Vivid Sydney vahvisti, että kaikki seuraaville kahdelle viikolle suunnitellut drooniesitykset perutaan.

## Ilotulitukset korvaavat droonit

Järjestäjien mukaan jäljellä olevien drooniesitysten tilalle tuodaan ilotulituksia, jotka täydentävät Darling Harbourissa järjestettävää Laser Lightfall -kokonaisuutta. Ilotulitukset ajoitetaan niihin ajankohtiin, joihin drooniesitykset oli aiemmin merkitty.

Vivid Sydneyn mukaan päätöksessä painoi yleisön, asukkaiden ja tapahtumakävijöiden turvallisuus sekä tarve antaa selkeä tieto ohjelman jatkosta festivaalin edetessä. Järjestäjät totesivat ymmärtävänsä, että peruutukset ovat yleisölle pettymys, mutta korostivat päätösten perustuvan asiantuntijoiden tekniseen ja viranomaisohjaukseen.

Tapaus ei lähteiden mukaan aiheuttanut henkilövahinkoja, mutta se johti koko drooniesityskokonaisuuden uudelleenarviointiin. Festivaali jatkuu muilta osin, ja Darling Harbourin iltaohjelmaa jatketaan muutetulla toteutuksella ilman drooneja.
